extracted.intended_audience: Parties and attorneys in FCC formal complaint proceedings; carriers and other applicants filing applications with the FCC (including cable landing license applicants).
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules governing (1) handling of confidential materials, filings, service, status conferences, accelerated docket, mediation, and review periods in formal complaint proceedings, and (2) filing, signing, amendment, defect, and specific-content requirements for carrier applications (including cable landing licenses) under FCC Part 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden for confidential designation challenges
rubrics_metrics.description: If a confidential designation is challenged, the party claiming confidentiality shall have the burden of demonstrating, by a preponderance of the evidence, that the materials designated as confidential fall under the standards for nondisclosure enunciated in the FOIA and that the designation is narrowly tailored to encompass only confidential information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This places the evidentiary burden on the proponent of confidentiality to show both statutory FOIA coverage and narrow tailoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public redacted filing of confidential materials
rubrics_metrics.description: File with the Commission, using the Commission's Electronic Comment Filing System, a public version of the materials that redacts any confidential information and clearly marks each page of the redacted public version with a header stating 'Public Version.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The redacted document shall be machine-readable whenever technically possible. If the document contains confidential metadata (e.g., privileged attorney-client metadata), the filer may remove such metadata before electronic filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unredacted confidential filing with Secretary
rubrics_metrics.description: File with the Secretary's Office an unredacted hard copy version of the materials that contains the confidential information and clearly marks each page of the unredacted confidential version with a header stating 'Confidential Version.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The unredacted version must be filed on the same day as the redacted version.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of hard copies of redacted and unredacted materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Serve one hard copy of the filed unredacted materials and one hard copy of the filed redacted materials on the attorney of record for each party to the proceeding, or, where a party is not represented by an attorney, each party to the proceeding either by hand delivery, overnight delivery, or email, together with a proof of such service in accordance with §§ 1.47(g) and 1.734(f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Service must include proof per cited sections; methods permitted include hand delivery, overnight delivery, or email.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorized recipients and limited use of confidential materials
rubrics_metrics.description: An attorney of record for a party or a party that receives unredacted materials marked as confidential may disclose such materials solely to specified persons (support personnel, officers/employees directly involved, consultants/expert witnesses, court reporters/stenographers), only for use in prosecuting or defending a party to the complaint action, and only to the extent necessary to assist in prosecution or defense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure is strictly limited to specified categories and limited-purpose use; unauthorized further disclosure is prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affirmation by individuals given access to confidential materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Each individual who is provided access to the information shall sign a declaration or affidavit stating that the individual has personally reviewed the Commission's rules and understands the limitations they impose on the signing party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an express, signed acknowledgement requirement for anyone granted access under the authorized-recipient rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies and logging of confidential materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may make copies of materials marked confidential solely for use by the Commission or persons designated in paragraph (b) of this section. Each party shall maintain a log recording the number of copies made of all confidential material and the persons to whom the copies have been provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain an auditable record of dissemination of confidential materials as part of compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protective orders
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may adopt a protective order with further restrictions as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission retains discretion to impose additional confidentiality protections beyond the base rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disposition and destruction of confidential materials upon termination
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon termination of a formal complaint proceeding, including all appeals and petitions, the parties shall ensure that all originals and reproductions of any confidential materials, along with the log recording persons who received copies of such materials, shall be provided to the producing party. In addition, upon final termination of the proceeding, any notes or other work product derived in whole or in part from the confidential materials of an opposing or third party shall be destroyed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obligation to return originals/reproductions and to destroy derived work product; applies after all appeals/petitions conclude.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission-directed briefs and inclusion of claims/defenses
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may require the parties to file briefs summarizing the facts and issues presented in the pleadings and other record evidence and presenting relevant legal authority and analysis. Unless otherwise directed, all briefs shall include all legal and factual claims and defenses previously set forth in the complaint, answer, or any other pleading submitted in the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission may limit scope of briefs to certain subjects. Omitting previously made claims/defenses from briefs has consequences (see abandonment rule).

rubrics_metrics.name: Abandonment of claims not reflected in briefs
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims and defenses previously made but not reflected in the briefs will be deemed abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all claims/defenses you wish considered are carried forward into required briefs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission may require additional information
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may require the parties to submit any additional information it deems appropriate for a full, fair, and expeditious resolution of the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to supplement the record on Commission request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status conference topics
rubrics_metrics.description: A status conference may include discussion of: (1) simplification or narrowing of the issues; (2) the necessity for or desirability of additional pleadings or evidentiary submissions; (3) obtaining admissions of fact or stipulations; (4) settlement of all or some matters by agreement; (5) whether discovery is necessary and, if so, the scope, type, and schedule for such discovery; (6) the schedule for the remainder of the case and dates for further status conferences; and (7) such other matters that may aid in disposition of the complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Status conferences are flexible and may address procedural narrowing, discovery, settlement, scheduling, and other case-management matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meet-and-confer and joint statement before initial status conference
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties shall meet and confer prior to the initial status conference to discuss settlement prospects, discovery, issues in dispute, schedules for pleadings, and prepare a joint statement of stipulated facts, disputed facts, and key legal issues; parties shall submit a joint statement of proposals agreed to and disputes remaining to Commission staff on a date specified by the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This obligation formalizes early case management and requires submission of a joint report to staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status conference procedures (requests, oral rulings, scheduling, failure to appear)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any party may request a status conference at any time after complaint filing. During a status conference, Commission staff may issue oral rulings on procedural matters, discovery, and submission of briefs or evidentiary materials. Status conferences will be scheduled by Commission staff at such time and place as it may designate (in person or by telephone). Failure to appear following reasonable notice will be deemed a waiver and will not preclude staff from conferring with those present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be timely in attendance and prepared for possible oral rulings; requests for additional conferences are allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on suing multiple defendants in one complaint
rubrics_metrics.description: Complaints may not be brought against multiple defendants unless they are commonly owned or controlled, are alleged to have acted in concert, are alleged to be jointly liable to complainant, or the complaint concerns common questions of law or fact. Complaints may, however, be consolidated by the Commission for disposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple-defendant complaints are limited to specified factual/legal relationships; consolidation remains a Commission discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee remittance and electronic filing of complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: The complainant shall remit separately the correct fee electronically, in accordance with part 1, subpart G (§ 1.1106) and shall file an original copy of the complaint using the Commission's Electronic Comment Filing System. If a complaint is addressed against multiple defendants, the complainant shall pay a separate fee for each additional defendant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electronic fee payment and ECFS filing are required where applicable; separate fees for additional defendants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of complaint on defendant the same day as filing
rubrics_metrics.description: The complainant shall serve the complaint by hand delivery on either the named defendant or one of the named defendant's registered agents for service of process on the same date that the complaint is filed with the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concurrent filing and service timing is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission notice to defendants and scheduling email
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt of the complaint by the Commission, the Commission shall promptly send, by email, to each defendant named in the complaint, notice of the filing of the complaint and shall additionally send by email to all parties a schedule detailing the date the answer and any other applicable pleading will be due and the date, time, and location of the initial status conference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission provides prompt electronic case notices and schedules to parties after filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of hard copies to Enforcement Bureau staff upon request
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties shall provide hard copies of all submissions to staff in the Enforcement Bureau upon request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even when filings are electronic, staff may request hard copies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic filing and service requirements for subsequent pleadings
rubrics_metrics.description: All subsequent pleadings and briefs filed in any formal complaint proceeding, as well as all letters, documents, or other written submissions, shall be filed using the Commission's Electronic Comment Filing System, excluding confidential material as set forth in § 1.731. In addition, all pleadings and briefs filed shall be served by the filing party on the attorney of record for each party or each unrepresented party by hand delivery, overnight delivery, or email, together with a proof of such service in accordance with § 1.47(g).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ECFS filing is the norm; confidential materials excluded from electronic filing per confidentiality rules; proof of service required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service timing rules (hand, overnight, email)
rubrics_metrics.description: Service by hand delivery delivered to recipient's office by 5:30 p.m. local time on a business day is deemed served that day; hand delivery after 5:30 p.m. is deemed served the next business day. Service by overnight delivery is deemed served the business day following acceptance by a reputable overnight delivery service. Service by email fully transmitted by 5:30 p.m. local time on a business day is deemed served that day; after 5:30 p.m. is deemed served the next business day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local-time 5:30 p.m. cutoff applies across service methods; plan filings/service accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental complaints filing fee exception
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplemental complaints filed pursuant to § 1.723 shall conform to the requirements set forth in § 1.734, except that the complainant need not submit a filing fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplemental complaints are otherwise subject to the same procedural requirements but are fee-exempt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct of proceedings (orders, decision on filings, informal meetings)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may issue such orders and conduct its proceedings as will best conduce to the proper dispatch of business and the ends of justice. The Commission may decide each complaint upon the filings and information before it, may request additional information from the parties, and may require one or more informal meetings with the parties to clarify the issues or to consider settlement of the dispute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad discretion to manage proceedings, request information, and use informal processes to reach resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accelerated Docket eligibility and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties to a formal complaint proceeding against a common carrier, or a pole attachment complaint proceeding against certain operators, may request inclusion on the Accelerated Docket; proceedings on the Accelerated Docket must be concluded within 60 days and are subject to shorter pleading deadlines and other procedural modifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain statutory or rule exceptions (47 U.S.C. 255, 617, 619, part 14) are excluded; accelerated timeline imposes stricter deadlines and potential procedural differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests and procedures to obtain Accelerated Docket treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: A complainant seeking inclusion shall submit a request to the Chief of the Enforcement Bureau's Market Disputes Resolution Division, by phone and in writing, prior to filing the complaint. Within five days of receiving service of any formal complaint against a common carrier (or specified defendants), a defendant may submit a similar request; defendants must contemporaneously transmit a copy to all parties. Commission staff has discretion to decide suitability and may require pre-filing settlement negotiations or mediation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely, dual-mode (phone + written) requests are required; staff discretion is central; mediation/settlement may be a precondition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accelerated Docket procedures (minitrial, removal, schedules, review)
rubrics_metrics.description: If accepted on the Accelerated Docket, staff will establish the schedule and process; staff may remove matters from the Accelerated Docket if inappropriate. The Commission may conduct a minitrial or trial-type hearing (no later than between 40 and 45 days after filing). Applications for review of staff decisions must comply with § 1.115(e)(4). For recommended decisions, comments challenging the decision must be filed within 15 days; oppositions within 15 days of those comments; reply comments may be filed 10 days thereafter and limited to issues raised. If no challenge to a recommended decision is filed, Commission will issue its decision adopting or modifying within 45 days of release; if comments are filed, decision issued within 30 days of final comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accelerated Docket creates compressed and fixed timelines for hearings and review; strict comment/response windows apply to recommended decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mediation availability and voluntariness
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission encourages parties to attempt to settle or narrow disputes. Enforcement Bureau staff are available to conduct mediations; staff will determine appropriateness. Participation is generally voluntary but may be required as a condition for inclusion on the Accelerated Docket.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties may request mediation before filing or while a proceeding is pending; staff discretion governs scheduling and materials requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to request mediation and pre-request verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may request mediation by calling the Chief of the Enforcement Bureau's Market Disputes Resolution Division, submitting a written request to the Chief, or including a mediation request in any pleading. Any party requesting mediation must verify that it has attempted to contact all other parties to determine whether they are amenable to mediation, and shall state the response of each party, if any.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests must include verification of outreach to other parties and their responses; staff consults with parties on scheduling and may request written statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abeyance pending mediation
rubrics_metrics.description: In any proceeding to which no statutory deadline applies, staff may, in its discretion, hold a case in abeyance pending mediation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mediation can pause proceedings where statutory deadlines are not implicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of mediation communications
rubrics_metrics.description: The parties and Commission staff shall keep confidential all written and oral communications prepared or made for purposes of the mediation (Mediation Communications). Neither staff nor the parties may use, disclose or seek to disclose Mediation Communications in any proceeding before the Commission or before any other tribunal, unless compelled to do so by law. Documents otherwise discoverable do not become Mediation Communications merely because they are disclosed or discussed during the mediation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communications made for mediation are protected from use in Commission proceedings and other tribunals absent compulsion by law; the mere discussion of discoverable documents in mediation does not render them confidential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination of mediation and continuing confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Any party or Commission staff may terminate a mediation by notifying other participants; staff shall promptly confirm in writing that the mediation has ended. The confidentiality rules continue to apply to Mediation Communications after termination. If staff ruled that the existence of mediation is confidential, that ruling continues after mediation ends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confidentiality protections survive termination of mediation; staff will confirm termination in writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for disputes under certain statutes and rules
rubrics_metrics.description: For disputes arising under 47 U.S.C. 255, 617, and 619, and the advanced communications services and equipment rules, parties shall submit the Request for Dispute Assistance in accordance with § 14.32 of this chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statute/rule-specific dispute-assistance procedures apply to these classes of disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: 271(d)(6)(B) complaints — waiver of 90-day resolution deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a complaint is filed pursuant to 47 U.S.C. 271(d)(6)(B), parties shall indicate whether they are willing to waive the 90 day resolution deadline either in the complaint and Formal Complaint Intake Form and defendant in its answer, or by indicating agreement at the initial status conference. Requests for waiver will not be entertained after the initial status conference absent a showing that waiver is in the public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Waiver must be affirmatively indicated at filing or at the initial status conference; late requests are highly restricted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary jurisdiction referrals procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Any party to a case involving claims under the Act that has been referred to the Commission by a court pursuant to the primary jurisdiction doctrine must contact the Market Disputes Resolution Division of the Enforcement Bureau for guidance before filing any pleadings or otherwise proceeding before the Commission. The Division will determine the procedural means by which the Commission will handle the referral. Failure to contact or to abide by Division determinations may result in dismissal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contacting the Division is mandatory prior to proceeding; noncompliance risks dismissal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review period for section 208 formal complaints (270-day expectation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Except in extraordinary circumstances, final action on a formal complaint filed pursuant to section 208 of the Act, and not governed by section 208(b)(1), should be expected no later than 270 days from the date the complaint is filed with the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Enforcement Bureau may pause the 270-day review period where actions outside the Commission's control unreasonably delay review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of application rules (§1.741)
rubrics_metrics.description: The general rules relating to applications contained in §§ 1.742 through 1.748 apply to all applications filed by carriers except those filed by public correspondence radio stations pursuant to parts 80, 87, and 101 of this chapter, and those filed by common carriers pursuant to part 25 of this chapter. Parts 21 and 101 contain general rules applicable to applications filed pursuant to these parts; see other parts as cross-referenced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-references to other parts may govern certain station types; check referenced parts for special rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place of filing, fees, and number of copies (§1.742)
rubrics_metrics.description: All applications which do not require a fee shall be filed electronically through the Commission's Electronic Comment Filing System if practicable. Applications which must be filed in hard copy format should be submitted according to the procedures set forth on the web page of the FCC's Office of the Secretary. Hand-delivered applications will be dated by the Secretary upon receipt (mailed applications will be dated by the Mail Branch). Applications accompanied by a fee payment should be filed in accordance with § 1.1105, Schedule of charges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default to ECFS when no fee applies; follow Secretary's Office instructions for hard copy submissions; dating depends on method of delivery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may sign applications (§1.743)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications, amendments, and related statements of fact must be signed by the applicant if an individual; by one of the partners if a partnership; by an officer or duly authorized employee if a corporation; or by a member who is an officer if an unincorporated association. Applications filed on behalf of eligible government entities must be signed by a duly elected or appointed official authorized under applicable law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signature authority varies by applicant type; ensure signatory has authority under relevant organizational law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attorney signature when applicant absent or disabled (§1.743(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications, amendments, and related statements may be signed by the applicant's attorney in case of the applicant's physical disability or absence from the United States. The attorney shall separately set forth the reason why the application is not signed by the applicant. If any matter is stated on the basis of the attorney's belief only (rather than his knowledge), he shall separately set forth his reasons for believing that such statements are true.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attorney-signing is allowed only with explained basis; statements made on attorney belief require explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original signature, sworn statements, and sanctions (§1.743(c)-(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Only the original of applications, amendments, or related statements of fact need be signed; copies may be conformed. Applications, amendments, and related statements need not be signed under oath. Willful false statements are punishable by fine and imprisonment (18 U.S.C. 1001) and administrative sanctions, including revocation of station license pursuant to section 312(a)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original signature required but not oath; false statements carry criminal and administrative penalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'Signed' and electronic signature allowance (§1.743(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Signed,' as used in this section, means an original hand-written signature, except that by public notice in the Federal Register the Wireline Competition Bureau may allow signature by any symbol executed or adopted by the applicant with the intent that such symbol be a signature, including symbols formed by computer-generated electronic impulses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default is hand-written original, but WCB can authorize nontraditional/electronic signature methods by public notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments to applications (§1.744)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any application not designated for hearing may be amended at any time by filing signed amendments in the same manner and with the same number of copies as the initial application. If a petition to deny (or to designate for hearing) has been filed, the amendment shall be served on the petitioner. After designation for hearing, requests to amend may be granted by the presiding officer upon good cause shown by petition, which petition shall be properly served upon all other parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amend freely pre-hearing; post-designation amendments require good-cause petition and service on parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orders to make applications more definite and certain (§1.744(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant may at any time be ordered to amend his application so as to make it more definite and certain. Such order may be issued upon motion of the Commission (or the presiding officer, if the application has been designated for hearing) or upon petition of any interested person, which petition shall be properly served.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission or presiding officer can compel clarification or specificity; interested parties may seek such orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional statements and documents requirement (§1.745)
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant may be required to submit such additional documents and written statements of fact, signed and verified (or affirmed), as in the judgment of the Commission (or the presiding officer, if designated for hearing) may be necessary. Any additional documents and written statements of fact required in connection with applications under Title II of the Communications Act need not be verified (or affirmed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission can demand supplemental verified statements; Title II applications have a verification exception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defective applications returned or accepted with waiver (§1.746)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications not in accordance with the applicable rules may be deemed defective and returned by the Commission without acceptance for filing and consideration. Such applications will be accepted for filing and consideration if accompanied by petition showing good cause for waiver of the rule with which the application does not conform. Assignment of a file number, if any, is for administrative convenience and does not indicate acceptance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nonconformance can lead to return unless a waiver petition demonstrates good cause; file number assignment is not acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inconsistent or conflicting applications (§1.747)
rubrics_metrics.description: When an application is pending or undecided, no inconsistent or conflicting application filed by the same applicant, his successor or assignee, or on behalf or for the benefit of said applicant, his successor, or assignee, will be considered by the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid filing later applications that conflict with a pending application by or for the same interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dismissal of applications before and after designation (§1.748)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before designation for hearing, any application not designated for hearing may be dismissed without prejudice at any time upon request of the applicant. A request for the return of an application accepted for filing but not designated for hearing will be deemed a request for dismissal without prejudice. The Commission may dismiss without prejudice when applicant fails to comply with requests for additional information. After designation for hearing, dismissal without prejudice is by petition and only for good cause; dismissal with prejudice after designation may occur when the applicant fails to comply with §1.221(c), otherwise fails to prosecute, or fails to comply with Commission requests for information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different standards apply pre- and post-designation; post-designation dismissals are more constrained and can be with prejudice for specified failures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action on applications under delegated authority (§1.749)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain applications do not require action by the Commission but, pursuant to delegated authority, may be acted upon by the Chief of the Wireline Competition Bureau subject to reconsideration by the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some applications are handled at bureau-chief level but remain subject to Commission reconsideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cable landing license application contents (§1.767(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications for cable landing licenses should contain: (1) the name, address and telephone number(s) of the applicant; (2) the Government, State, or Territory under whose laws each corporate or partnership applicant is organized; (3) the name, title, post office address, and telephone number of the officer/contact for correspondence; (4) a description of the submarine cable, including the type and number of channels and capacity; (5) a specific description of the cable landing stations with a map showing geographic coordinates (initial general description allowed but final specific description required 90 days prior to construction, with public notice and Commission approval timing specified); (6) statement whether cable will be operated on a common carrier or non-common carrier basis; (7) a list of proposed owners of the cable system with voting and ownership interests; (8) for each applicant, place of organization and certifications required in § 63.18(h),(o),(p),(q); (9) certification as to whether applicant is or is affiliated with a foreign carrier specifying each country; (10) a certification as to whether the applicant seeks to land/operate a submarine cable connecting the U.S. to any country for which specified foreign-carrier-control/ownership conditions apply and related detail; and (11) a certification accepting routine conditions and any other information necessary to enable the Commission to act on the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes a special note about Coastal Zone Management Act consistency certifications and cross-references to § 63.10(a) market-power criteria for non-WTO countries. If applying for assignment/transfer, applicant must include pre- and post-transaction ownership diagrams, narrative describing transfer, and specify percentage voting/ownership interests by segment; transferee completes specified paragraphs.
